summary: The reviewed candidate preserves useful long-prefix reuse by inserting a genuinely captured grid-aligned checkpoint, but it does not fix the original three-token n-1 case: [A,B,C] followed by [A,B] still returns zero. That result is required because the only stored recurrent state belongs to depth 3, and the architecture cannot separately replay recurrent layers for KV-only hits. Exact nonzero reuse requires an exact depth-2 recurrent+convolution checkpoint or a new split-replay execution path.

tests.what_was_measured: 20 tests passed. The exact [A,B,C] then [A,B] lookup returned 0; the full leaf retained ownership; a real depth-64 checkpoint returned 64; divergence before the first checkpoint returned 0. Existing Mamba cache tests remained green.

tests.what_was_measured: 19 tests passed. The candidate's own exact short-prefix test and the independent ownership test both asserted a zero-token hit, while explicitly checkpointed long prefixes returned 64.

On the assigned AMD Instinct MI350X, actual MambaRadixCache GPU tensors returned 0 indices for the short n-1 split, 3 for the full owned leaf, and 64 for a real checkpoint; full and checkpointed results exactly matched independent torch.arange GPU references.
No whitespace errors in the delivered changes.

remaining_limitations: No hybrid-Mamba model weights were prepared, so end-to-end logits and latency were not measured. Exact n-1 reuse below the first checkpoint remains unsupported without arbitrary-depth recurrent+convolution snapshotting or a split-replay execution path. The candidate's long-prefix improvement was verified but is not included because it does not solve the reviewed original case.
